title: ReAct execution loop
content: Operate as Think → Act → Observe. Before each tool call, state your goal in 1 line. After each result, state what you learned and your next step. If a tool fails, immediately try: (1) different parameters, (2) different tool, (3) different source. Never retry the exact same call twice.

title: Video download execution
content: For video downloads: 1) Use download_video with the URL directly — it handles YouTube, TikTok, Twitter, Instagram. 2) If download_video fails, use run_python with yt-dlp: install it, then run 'yt-dlp -f best URL -o /tmp/video.mp4'. 3) Verify with run_terminal 'ls -la /tmp/video.mp4 && ffprobe /tmp/video.mp4'. 4) Return get_sandbox_file_url. Never browse the video page first — it wastes a tool call.

title: Web research and identification
content: For identifying something by description: 1) First search uses the MOST UNIQUE details (character names, specific scenes, unusual features) — not generic descriptions. 2) Target Reddit, MAL, forums with 'identify' or 'help find' in query. 3) If first search fails, try a completely different angle: a different language (use the original-language terms when applicable), a different detail subset, or browse a promising thread. 4) After 3 failed searches, present closest matches and ask 1-2 narrowing questions (year range, art style, platform where they saw it). Never rephrase same keywords.

title: Code execution in sandbox
content: For code/file tasks in E2B sandbox: 1) Install packages first with install_packages (don't check if installed). 2) Write and run code in one step — don't split into write then run. 3) For file outputs, always verify with 'ls -la path' before calling get_sandbox_file_url. 4) For data processing, prefer pandas/polars. For images, prefer Pillow. For PDFs, prefer reportlab or pypdf. 5) If a library fails, try the alternative immediately (e.g., openpyxl → xlsxwriter).

title: Mobile app sourcing
content: For app requests: 1) Use app_source tool first — it handles both Play Store and App Store lookups. 2) If app_source doesn't have it, search_web for 'appname APK download site:apkpure.com OR site:apkmirror.com'. 3) For iOS, provide App Store link since direct IPA download isn't practical. 4) Always prefer official sources. If the app is paid, provide the store link — don't search for cracked versions.

title: File format conversion
content: For file conversions: 1) Identify input/output formats. 2) Choose tool: ffmpeg for audio/video, Pillow for images, pandoc for documents, reportlab for PDF creation, pypdf for PDF manipulation. 3) Install the needed package, run conversion in one Python script, verify output exists. 4) Common patterns: 'ffmpeg -i input.mp4 output.mp3' for video→audio, 'from PIL import Image; img.save("out.png")' for image conversion.

title: Browser automation tasks
content: For browser-based tasks: 1) Use browse_web first to read page content. 2) Only use browser_interact when you need to: click buttons, fill forms, navigate dynamically-loaded content, or interact with SPAs. 3) Use screenshot_analyze to verify visual state when unsure. 4) For login flows: fill credentials → submit → verify success via page content change. 5) Never store or display credentials in chat.

title: Search efficiency rules
content: Search efficiency: 1) For simple facts (who/what/when), use AT MOST 1 search. If snippets answer it, respond immediately. 2) For current data (prices, versions, scores), 1 search is enough — use the most authoritative snippet. 3) Never do a second search to 'verify' a simple fact. 4) Prefer search snippets over browsing full pages. 5) If you know the answer from training data and it's not time-sensitive, answer WITHOUT any search.

title: Non-English language interaction
content: When the user writes in a non-English language: 1) Reply in the same language unless they explicitly switch. 2) For searches, try both the original-language terms and an English transliteration / translation when the topic is region-specific. 3) For text-processing code, respect the script's Unicode ranges and use established libraries (e.g. ICU, language-specific tokenizers, deep-translator) rather than ad-hoc regex. 4) Be aware that some scripts have legacy encodings (e.g. older fonts vs Unicode); normalize to Unicode before processing. 5) Never assume English is the default — preserve the user's language choice in the final answer.

title: Common error recovery
content: Error recovery decision tree: Network timeout → retry once. 404/not found → try alternative URL or source. Permission denied → try different library or approach. Import error → install the package first. File not found → check path with ls, fix path. Rate limited (429) → wait 2s then retry. SSL error → try with verify=False or alternative URL. Memory error → process in chunks or use streaming.

title: File and artifact delivery
content: When delivering files to user: 1) Always verify the file exists and has non-zero size before calling get_sandbox_file_url. 2) Place the download URL at the END of your response, clearly labeled. 3) Include file size and format info. 4) Never re-share URLs from previous turns. 5) For multiple files, consider zipping them first with manage_sandbox_files.

title: Data analysis execution
content: For data analysis: 1) Read the file first to understand structure (head, dtypes, shape). 2) Use pandas for tabular data, numpy for numerical. 3) For charts, use matplotlib or plotly — save as PNG/HTML. 4) For large files (>100MB), use chunked reading or polars. 5) Always show key findings in text before delivering chart files. 6) Common pattern: pd.read_csv → describe() → specific analysis → visualization → save → deliver URL.

title: Security and credential handling
content: Security rules: 1) Never ask users to paste API keys, tokens, or passwords in chat. 2) Never print environment variables, Authorization headers, or session cookies in responses. 3) If a tool needs auth, use the tool's built-in auth mechanism. 4) For API requests, reference credentials by variable name, never by value. 5) If you accidentally see a secret in tool output, do NOT repeat it in your response.

title: Media file inspection
content: For media files: 1) Inspect with ffprobe (video/audio) or identify/exiftool (images). 2) Never dump raw binary content to chat. 3) For audio analysis: ffprobe -v quiet -print_format json -show_format -show_streams file.mp3. 4) For video info: ffprobe -v quiet -print_format json -show_format file.mp4. 5) For image info: python 'from PIL import Image; img = Image.open(f); print(img.size, img.format)'.

title: Direct API requests
content: For API requests: 1) Use http_request when you know the exact endpoint and don't need browser rendering. 2) Set appropriate headers (Content-Type, Accept). 3) For paginated APIs, fetch only what's needed — don't loop through all pages unless asked. 4) Parse JSON responses in the tool output — don't make a second call just to format. 5) If API returns error, check: auth headers, URL encoding, request body format.
